title: Everest Pipkin - Dungeons, Digging, and Wells - the Gamers Yearn for the Mines.
speaker: Everest Pipkin
talk_title: Dungeons, Digging, and Wells - the Gamers Yearn for the Mines.
description:
“He looked into the hole, and like any hole it said, Jump.”

— Susan Sontag, The Volcano Lover: A Romance

This wide-ranging but decidedly subterranean 30 minute talk covers a variety of approaches to digital holes in games, as well as the actions of mining / digging / tunneling that cause them. It considers the undergrounds as caught up in varied histories of extraction, labor, devotion, gambling, travel and desire, as well as looks at video game digging across multiple end goals such as "finding treasure", "changing the landscape", or "progressing and moving through the dark". Finally, it considers the subterranean fantasy of buried and alien worlds, where the rules are different than on the surface of the earth– and what that can and has meant to a long history of games that ask you to delve.
